title: TypeScript SDK: stream-union shim for graceful cancellation and partial-result merging
creator: Alex Moreno
description:
Problem: Consumers of the TS SDK need ergonomic, predictable behavior when interoperating between AsyncIterator-based codepaths and Web Streams (ReadableStream). Current helpers cover one-way conversions but leave gaps: cancellation semantics differ, partial/delta token outputs need merging for deterministic final values, and backpressure semantics can break real-time UIs or server-side batching.

Goal: Implement a small runtime shim ("stream-union") that: 1) accepts either an AsyncIterable or ReadableStream source and exposes both consumption models; 2) normalizes cancellation signals across both worlds (AbortSignal <-> iterator.return() <-> stream.cancel()); 3) emits structured partial events and a final merged result; 4) preserves backpressure where possible and exposes configuration to prioritize latency vs throughput.

Why now: Multiple customers and internal examples (console streaming logs, reranker streaming, and long-prompt assistants) surfaced edge cases where UI components lost partial state or observed duplicate tail tokens after retries. This ticket proposes an SDK-first shim that standardizes behavior so apps don't need bespoke adapters.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change runtime server behavior or add new network protocols. It only implements client-side shim and accompanying docs/examples and tests.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a lightweight helper 'streamUnion' that accepts AsyncIterable<T> | ReadableStream<T> and returns { asyncIterable, readableStream, abortController }
Cancellation from any surface must close the other surface: calling readableStream.cancel() aborts the AsyncIterable consumer and vice versa
Partial/delta events are emitted as 'patch' events and the shim produces a final merged object event; finalization semantics work for both pull (iterator) and push (webstream) consumers
Backpressure mapping preserves consumer pacing: when iterator consumer is slow, ReadableStream backpressure signals should reduce producer throughput instead of unbounded buffering
Unit tests covering race between cancel and finalization, tests for partial merges, and an integration test in example app that demonstrates UI correctness
Documentation and one example in examples/ts/stream-union-demo showing conversion patterns and recommended knobs (latencyMode vs throughputMode)
technical_notes: Design: shim will wrap incoming source in an internal controller that tracks subscribers and a single producer loop. The loop reads from the source and fans events into both an AsyncGenerator and a ReadableStream sink implementation.

Cancellation mapping: create an AbortController per shim. Hook to iterator.return() by intercepting generator and calling abortController.abort(). For ReadableStream consumer, implement cancel(reason) -> abortController.abort(reason). Producer reads should observe abortSignal and gracefully stop fetching/consuming incremental tokens.

Partial merging: define small lightweight 'Patch' type and a mergePartial(patches[]) strategy. For common text streams, the merge is append-with-de_dup. For structured JSON diffs we expose a pluggable mergeFn option. The default mergeFn handles arrays and top-level text patches.

Backpressure: implement a small bounded in-memory queue (configurable default 8 chunks). When queue is full and consumer is slow, the producer's next read is paused via await onBackpressure() which resolves when queue drains. For ReadableStream we implement pull() semantics and for iterator we yield from the queue.
API ergonomics: export helpers: fromAsyncIterable, fromReadableStream, toAsyncIterable, toReadableStream, and streamUnion factory that wires both endpoints.
Performance: avoid copying large chunks; pass references and only clone if consumer requests slice. Measure allocations in unit tests.
code_examples: // Typical usage: consume as AsyncIterator or ReadableStream from the same source
for await (const patch of asyncIterable) { uiState.applyPatch(patch); if (shouldStop) { await asyncIterable.return(); } }

const reader = readableStream.getReader();
    while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; renderPatch(value); }
const merged = streamUnion(source, { mergeFn: (acc, patch) => customMerge(acc, patch), queueSize: 16 });
comments: 2026-02-10 Alex Moreno: Created ticket with problem statement and proposed API surface. Punted deep docs until API stabilizes. Linked to initial customer bug reports.

2026-02-16 Priya Kapoor (Design review): Prefer exposing a single factory over multiple conversion helpers to reduce user confusion. Suggested default 'balanced' mode where queueSize=8 and mergeFn default is text-append. Design suggested small README example for both iterator and stream consumers.

2026-02-20 Ethan Zhao: Spike implemented prototype in branch feat/stream-union-spike. Verified basic iterator->stream forwarding and cancellation mapping. Observed 2-3% allocation overhead vs native conversion at small chunk sizes. Push to refine backpressure semantics.

2026-02-25 Ben Liu (QA): Added test plan items for race conditions (cancel during mid-patch), large patch streaming (>1MB), and memory growth under slow consumer. Found issue where readableStream.cancel() did not signal generator.return() in node16 runtime — added node-specific polyfill in spike.

2026-03-03 Code review (PR #6832): Feedback from reviewers to expose 'latencyMode' boolean for immediate flush of partials vs batch-merge. Also requested stronger TypeScript generics on mergeFn. I updated types and added tests.
2026-03-08 Integration test: wired streamUnion into examples/ts/stream-union-demo and validated UI didn't show duplicate tail tokens after a retry. Observed improved UX in chat composer demo.

2026-03-12 Ethan Zhao: Marking ticket In Progress — preparing PR to main with follow-up item for feature flagging 'latencyMode' for staged rollout. Planning to cut release sdk-2026.03 once QA signoff is complete.
testing_plan: Unit tests for conversion helpers, cancellation races, and partial merge correctness. Integration test in examples/ts validates UI rendering. Performance microbench that measures allocations and end-to-end latency under 3 consumer profiles (fast iterator, slow iterator, fast reader). Run on node16 and node20 matrix CI. QA to run manual flow for chat composer and reranker streaming.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'streamUnion' opt-in in SDK alpha. Release as SDK beta under sdk-2026.03. Enable by default for examples only for first week, flip flag after monitoring errors and memory metrics for 48h. If regressions occur, revert flag and publish quick patch. Post-rollback postmortem if >1 customer impact.
risks: Edge-case mismatch between Node and Browser stream semantics causing leak in Node 16 (polyfills included but need CI validation)
Large patch composition could create latency spikes if mergeFn is synchronous and CPU heavy
Incorrect backpressure mapping may degrade throughput for server-side batching workloads
metrics: streaming.finalized_rate: percentage of streams that emit final merged event within 10s
streaming.dup_tail_rate: rate of duplicate tail tokens observed in UI tests
memory.heap_delta_per_stream: average heap growth per active stream over 60s
